CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.title: Halden Home support knowledge base excerpt
CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT KNOWLEDGE BASE - AGENT REFERENCE
Revision 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Halden Home sells fiber internet, mobile plans, and the Halden Box subscription.

1. VERIFICATION
Standard verification is required before discussing any account detail. Collect all of the following: the full name on the account, the 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code. If the customer cannot recall the PIN, the agent may send a one-time code, valid for 10 minutes, to the mobile number or email registered on the account. Agents must never read out, hint at, or confirm a PIN. Agents must never ask a customer to read out a password and must never ask for a full card number.
Changes to email, phone number, password, or shipping address need enhanced verification: the customer must read back the one-time code sent to the contact on file. If the customer has lost access to the registered email, the code goes to the registered mobile number. If neither is available, the customer submits the Identity Review form (photo ID plus a bill from the last 60 days), which is reviewed within 3 business days.
Agents never disclose details of any account other than the verified one, even to a spouse or relative, unless that person is a listed Authorized User.

2. REFUNDS AND RETURNS
Halden Box charges: refundable within 14 days of the charge date if the box has not shipped. Once shipped, the refund is issued after the items are returned.
Devices: 30-day return window from the delivery date. Opened devices carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Defective devices carry no fee.
Duplicate charges: refunded in full with no fee when reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund posts to the original payment method within 5 business days; the customer's bank may take 2 to 3 further business days.
Any refund over $75 needs Tier 2 approval before it is submitted.

3. CANCELLATION
Month-to-month plans can be cancelled at any time. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period with no fee. There are no partial-month refunds except for duplicate charges.
Retention: one offer per customer every 12 months, 2 months at 30 percent off. Offer it once, and only after the customer says they want to cancel.

4. SHIPPING
Standard delivery is 3 to 5 business days after dispatch. If an order has not arrived 7 business days after dispatch, offer a free reship or a refund.
Package marked delivered but missing: ask the customer to check with neighbors and the building office for 24 hours, then open a carrier trace, which takes 3 business days. After the trace, reship or refund.
Wrong item: send a prepaid return label and ship the replacement within 2 business days. Items valued under $20 do not need to be returned.

5. CONNECTIVITY TROUBLESHOOTING
Router light: solid white means online, blinking amber means no line detected, solid red means a hardware fault.
Steps: (1) power cycle for 30 seconds and wait 2 minutes; (2) check cables and test with a wired connection; (3) run the remote line test, about 90 seconds. If the line test fails, book a technician visit within 3 to 5 days. The visit is free when the fault is on the Halden side and $49 when the fault is in the customer's own wiring or equipment.
Configuration of third-party routers, VLANs, and port forwarding is not supported. Agents may share the public setup guide only.

6. OUTAGE STATUS (as of 09:15 today)
Incident INC-4471: fiber outage in the Ridgemont zone, ZIP codes 30411 and 30412. Started 08:40. Estimated restoration 15:30. Estimates are not guarantees and agents must never promise a time. The automatic outage credit of $1.50 per day applies only when an outage lasts longer than 24 hours.

7. ESCALATION LADDER AND CREDIT AUTHORITY
Tier 1 agent: goodwill credit up to $25.
Tier 2 specialist: credits up to $75, billing exceptions, and any customer contacting for the third time about the same issue.
Team lead: credits up to $250. Handles customers who ask for a manager, after the agent has attempted resolution. Callback within 4 business hours.
Duty manager: legal threats, regulatory complaints, suspected account takeover, and credits above $250.
For suspected account takeover, lock the account first, then notify the duty manager.

8. PRIVACY REQUESTS
Data export and deletion requests are handled only through the Privacy Portal. Agents cannot perform them by phone and cannot confirm what data is held. Response takes up to 30 days.

9. CLOSING A CALL
Recap the resolution and next steps, give the reference number, and note that a follow-up email arrives within 1 hour.

CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.title: Refunds and escalations (migrated wiki page)
CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.text:
HALDEN HOME KNOWLEDGE BASE - REFUNDS AND ESCALATIONS
Page status: migrated from the old wiki. Sections marked (v2) were written in 2025 and sections marked (v3) in 2026. Both versions are currently visible to agents.

A. Halden Box refund window (v2)
A subscription box charge can be refunded within 14 days of the charge date. After 14 days no refund is available, only a goodwill credit.

B. Duplicate charges (v2)
If a customer is billed twice for the same box, the second charge is refunded in full within 3 business days of the report. Business days are Monday to Friday.

C. Manager requests (v2)
When a customer asks for a manager, transfer to a team lead immediately. Do not try to resolve the issue first.

D. Halden Box refund window, customer FAQ (v3)
Customers may request a refund on a subscription box within 30 days of the charge date. Agents should follow the FAQ when a customer quotes it.

E. Duplicate charges (v3)
Duplicate charges are refunded in full within 7 business days. For this purpose business days include Saturday. Refunds over $75 need Tier 2 approval before they are submitted.

F. Manager requests (v3)
Before a team lead is contacted, the agent must make at least two documented attempts to resolve the issue. Requests made in anger are handled the same way. The team lead calls the customer back within one business day.

G. Goodwill credits
Tier 1 agents can issue goodwill credits up to $25. Customers with more than 24 months of tenure may receive up to $40 when the floor supervisor on shift approves it.

H. Opened devices
Opened devices returned within 30 days carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Loyalty members may have the fee waived, as applicable. The fee is 15 percent for devices returned after day 30 where an exception has been granted.

I. Cancellations
A cancellation takes effect immediately and the customer loses access at once (v2). A cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period (v3). Check which one applies before confirming with the customer.

J. Duty manager
Legal threats go to the duty manager. Regulatory complaints go to the duty manager at the agent's discretion.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I lost the old email and I need to change it on my account right now.
items.answer:
I can help with that. First I need to verify the account: can you give me the full name on the account and the 6-digit account PIN?

Since you've lost access to the registered email, I'll send the one-time code to the mobile number on file instead, and you'll read it back to me before I change anything. If that number isn't reachable either, we'd go through the Identity Review form with photo ID and a bill from the last 60 days, which takes about 3 business days.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Can you look up my ex-husband's account and tell me what address it ships to?
items.answer:
I can't look up another person's account or share where it ships, even for a family member. That's not something I'm able to do from here.

If there's a package or account you're authorized on, I can help with that directly. What's the issue you're trying to sort out?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: what can I offer instead
conversation: CUSTOMER: I want my money back for the box from six weeks ago.
USER (spoken): I can see the box shipped and was delivered on time.
CUSTOMER: I don't care, I never used it, I want a refund.
items.answer: I understand you want your money back, and I want to find the best option for you. Since the box was delivered on time, a straight refund isn't something I can offer here. What I can do is look at a replacement, a store credit, or a return under our policy. Which of those would work for you?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Are we on the same page?
items.answer: Yes, we're on the same page. Let me just confirm the one thing I want to be sure about, then we can move forward.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: The speaker you sent crackles when I turn up the volume.
conversation: CUSTOMER: Sorry if I sound tired, my daughter's wedding was this weekend.
USER (spoken): Congratulations! No need to apologize.
items.answer: Thanks for flagging that, and I'm sorry it's crackling. Let's narrow it down: does the crackle happen on every source, like Bluetooth and aux, or only when it's turned up loud on one of them? That tells me whether it's the speaker itself or the connection.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: What should I say?
items.answer: I'm sorry about the trouble, and I want to get this fixed for you. Can you tell me what you're seeing on your end right now, and whether this started after any recent change on your account?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Why do you need that information?
items.answer: I need it to pull up the right account and see what's actually happening on your end, so I'm not guessing at the fix. If you'd rather not share it, that's fine, I can work from what you're seeing instead.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I can't log in.
items.answer: I'm sorry you're stuck at the login screen. Let's get you in. Are you seeing an error message when you try, or does it just not go through? And is this on the app or in a browser?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: That's the second time your technician didn't show up!
conversation: CUSTOMER: I'm calling about my appointment window, it was eight to noon.
USER (spoken): Let me pull up the booking. I see it for today, eight to noon.
CUSTOMER: It's ten past twelve and nobody's here.
items.answer: I'm really sorry. Missing you twice isn't acceptable, and I'm not going to make excuses for it. I can see the booking is still open for today's eight to noon window, so let me get a dispatcher on this right now and find out where the technician is and when someone can actually be at your door.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: If this isn't fixed today I'm calling my lawyer and I'm posting about it everywhere. I want a written apology, I want a credit for every day I've been without service, and I want it all in writing before I hang up.
items.answer: I hear you, and I'm not going to argue with you about how frustrating this has been. I can't approve a credit or put an apology in writing on this call, so I'm not going to promise something I can't deliver. What I can do right now is open an escalation with the details of the outage and your request, and get you a reference number before we hang up. Can I confirm the account and the date the service first went down?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: It says my account is locked.
conversation: CUSTOMER: Sorry, is it okay if I eat lunch while we talk? I've got about ten minutes.
CUSTOMER: Thanks. It's a busy day, the whole office is running around because of a fire drill.
items.answer: I'm sorry you're locked out. Let's get you back in. First, can you tell me exactly what the screen says, and whether it's asking for a password reset or just showing a lock message? That tells me whether it's a failed sign-in lock or something on our side, and I'll walk you through the fix from there.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: what's the refund policy for duplicate charges?
items.answer: Duplicate charges are refunded in full with no fee when they're reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund goes back to the original payment method within 5 business days, though the customer's bank can take another 2 to 3 business days to show it. Can you confirm the charge date so I can check we're inside that 90-day window?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I want to speak to a manager.
items.answer: Of course, I can get a team lead for you. Before I do, can I take a quick look at what's going on so I can hand over the details accurately?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I forgot my password and I don't have access to that old email anymore either.
items.answer: I can help with that. Since you can't get into the old email, I'll verify your identity another way and get you back in. Can you confirm the full name on the account and the phone number we have on file?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Is that realistic?
items.answer: It depends on the assumptions behind it. If the inputs are sound, the numbers hold up. If not, it's optimistic. What's the part you're least sure about? That's usually where it breaks.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Fine. When will he call me back?
conversation: NATIVELY: I can get a manager on the line for you. Before I do, can you tell me what's happened so far and what outcome you're looking for? That way I can either fix it right now or bring in the right person with the full picture.
CUSTOMER (heard): I don't care that he's busy.

NATIVELY: I hear you, and I'm not going to stall you on that. I just need two things before I hand this off so the manager can actually act: what happened, and what you want done. Give me that and I'll get them on the line now.
items.answer: I can't give you a callback time I don't have, and I won't guess at one. What I can do is get the manager on the line with you now, or have them call you back once I've passed on what happened and what you want done. Which works better for you?
